items.item_text: Job offer is contingent upon satisfactory clearance based on Background Check results.
This position requires a minimum of three (3) days/week on campus/on-site.
Cover letter required for a complete application.

Under the general direction of the Assistant Dean and Chief Financial and Administrative Officer, the Director of Academic Personnel (AP) & Human Resources (HR)provides leadership and oversight for the Jacobs School Deans Office AP & HR Service Center or Engineering. The Director is responsible for developing and executing a responsive, consistent, and customer-focused service model that supports the School’s academic departments, faculty, and leadership.

Responsible for overseeing the shared service model (AP/HR) for the school. Establish operational objectives and work plans, and delegate assignments to subordinate managers. Responsible for managing, preparing, administering, and directing resources and making recommendations for functional change. Director will monitor and ensure adherence to deans annual budget. Incumbent will be involved in developing, modifying and executing organizational policies that affect immediate operation(s) and may also have organization-wide effect. Erroneous decisions or failure to achieve goals results in additional costs and personnel, and serious delays in overall schedules. Responsible for service delivery, risk, staffing, and resource allocation. The decisions recommended by incumbent impact six departments and have significant compliance, financial, employee-relations, and reputational consequences.

The Director serves as a key partner for school leadership and with other central campus offices. The incumbent will build strong relationships with departments, develop a thorough understanding of their AP and HR staff needs, and ensure that faculty and department administrators receive timely, accurate, and solutions-oriented support. The Director will help departments navigate complex policies and processes while balancing the need for schoolwide consistency with legitimate differences in departmental operations and priorities. The individual will ensure cross functional integration of work so the Academic HR team collaborates effectively with the Staff HR team to resolve overlapping personnel issues (e.g., employees holding both staff and academic appointments)This position is responsible for coordinating academic personnel and staff HR operations to create an integrated service model with clear accountability, effective escalation pathways, and a strong customer-service experience.

The incumbent provides support and oversight to the consolidated Academic Personnel team. The Director working with the Academic Personnel Associate Director will establish clear service expectations, operating procedures, communication protocols, escalation pathways, and performance measures. The position will regularly assess workloads, case status, turnaround times, service quality, and customer feedback to identify and implement opportunities for improvement. The Director oversees a broad range of academic personnel activities, which may include faculty recruitment and appointment, academic review and advancement, compensation, leaves, separations, and other complex or sensitive faculty matters. The incumbent is expected to exercise sound judgment, maintain strict confidentiality, identify and mitigate risk, and provide clear guidance regarding University and campus policies.

The incumbent will also provide leadership and oversight for the consolidated staff human resource team within the consolidated model, working closely with department leadership and central Human Resources on recruitment, classification and compensation, employee relations, performance management, leave administration, and workforce planning. The manager will promote consistent and equitable HR practices across the School while ensuring departments receive responsive, solutions-oriented support.

Direct the School’s administrative consolidation efforts by leading employees and stakeholders through organizational and process transitions with transparency, empathy, and accountability. Utilize comprehensive Academic Personnel (AP) and Human Resources (HR) expertise, combined with change management, operational, and relationship-building skills, to foster a collaborative, approachable, and customer-service-driven leadership environment.
~ Cover letter required for a complete application.
Broad knowledge of complex personnel, compensation, and related policies and procedures for academic employees.
Requires a strong understanding of the organizational structure and responsibilities of unit.
Requires understanding of HR and related databases.
Ability to develop creative solutions which may have no precedent.
Requires innovation, in-depth knowledge of organizational and university policies and operational procedures.
Strong decision making, analytical, problem solving, critical thinking and resource management skills.

Understanding of applicable Academic Personnel and HR staff, union contracts and collective bargaining agreements, with the ability to interpret and apply contract provisions to daily personnel operation. Comfortable navigating multi-unit bargaining environments and advising leadership on compliance and labor relations matters
